What are some things I should avoid doing if I want the 'best experience?' For example, I know you should wait to do Chika's Schadenfreude event until after the Beach event, are there any other situations like that I should avoid?
Click to expand...
As far as I know just that one, every other lockout is either due to not having enough affection/lust or is an explicit choice (like Ami's lust events). One thing I'd suggest is making a new save each time a new girl appears, you have a choice to make, or you open up someone's lust events. While there's only one case of being locked out of one girl's events based on choices made with other girls, I have every expectation there are more to come (there's likely to be some consequence with Sana for sleeping with Sara first, for example).

Vizer007 said:
So...How many hours of gameplay it there?
Click to expand...
If you read through everything I would guess 20-40 hours, depending on how fast you are and whether you're using a walkthrough. Between reading, grinding stats, and searching for happy scenes/exploring alternate paths this game has a LOT of content and that's only going to keep expanding. That's why I'd suggest keeping a lot of saves.

Lucas Martinez said:
Well, a lot of pregnant girls would make the rest of the story pretty difficult, but maybe there's a way around that. I mean the world keeps getting reset, with changes each time, so maybe there's an opportunity to fit it in that way. I don't see it as likely either though
Click to expand...
There might be a way around that, but there is no way around the resets pushing time back to before the pregnancy and there's no telling if enough time will pass for it to show before the end of the game or a reset pushes time back to before it was showing. Even if they get pregnant, if time gets reset back to before they were impregnated or before they were showing, it might as well not be there.

Even then, if the time frame of the game is too short, it won't have time to develop to the point of showing in that case, either. Remember that there is no magic in this game world except maybe a supernatural force irresistibly compelling player Sensei to act at certain points, the Yumi kiss is a perfect example of this, so there is no way to speed up pregnancy, especially without harming the mother in the process. This makes pregnancy impossible to do from a story perspective unless there is enough time going by in the game for a pregnancy to develop naturally, which is roughly nine months.

I see no indication this game will span nine months of events even with the development taking multiple years by design.

There's also the elephant in the room, player Sensei is trying, and apparently failing, to keep his multiple sexual relationships a secret. Not every girl is aware he is seeing others or how many he is seeing at this point, but some do know he is seeing at least one other girl and several know that other girls feel that way toward him. Ayane and Ami are particularly dangerous in that regard and Sana, being the quiet girl, is also one to watch out for. Kirin is openly manipulative and has evidence that could end at least one relationship, his relationship with Ayane, instantly, so even if she truly has no real intention to cause trouble with that evidence like she says, we can't rule out her acting out of emotion and exposing them without meaning to.

Any of the girls becoming pregnant with really only one guy around that could pull that off because of the war is an instant red flag and player Sensei would be an instant prime suspect because he is so close to them.

I'm sure this comment will be mostly ignored, but it's been bothering me so I'm posting it anyway. I enjoy this game a lot, it's well written in general, and the characters are diverse and well thought out.
Except for one glaring error - Molly. It's not too much of a stretch to guess the dev's probably American, but I have to say, as an actual Irish person, Molly's character is almost painful. There's a section where you brought up stereotypes, and the effects they have. Well, unfortunately you've fallen into them. Molly talks like a Scot, the stereotypes you've brought up are American stereotypes, and in Japan, the most common issue Irish people run into are "Isn't that part of England?", and "That's the country beside Greenland, right?"
This is probably a really minor issue for you, I just wanted to bring it up because her stories actually make me uncomfortable, she's that far off.

In case you're curious of a few things - red hair is actually still super rare in Ireland. Americans call it the Emerald Isle, actual Irish people only do that for tourists. The majority religion is catholic, and almost nobody follows ancient celtic superstitions, not even in our super-old Irish Only Area. I haven't seen you do it, but about 85% of Ireland doesn't speak Irish fluently, it's largely a dead language. (Edit: I've never been proven wrong so fast. The only person I've ever heard attempt curse in Irish is my long-dead great-grandfather who fought in the Rising)

I don't expect a reply, or even for anyone to actually read this comment, I just wanted to get it out there, especially since there's an actual section of her plot about stereotyping being bad, while her character is also a bad stereotype. Perhaps there's some poetic irony there.

A suggestion for when you return, for a minor QoL tweak to your already far above-average UX. Unseen events which feature H-scenes seem to be marked with a pink color, but this is no longer visible once the event is unlocked. There is no way to distinguish them from other already-seen events as-of now (unless this is already fixed in the patreon-only version).

The limited amount of colours to use in the palette of the game makes it a bit hard to have it be both intuitive, aesthetically pleasing and easily discernible, but even something as simple as changing the color of the highlighted event when hovering over it from (its current) pink, reserving pink highlights for events with H-scenes would be an improvement (since there isn't enough event clutter for each girl that hovering over each event and checking takes more than a few seconds). Personally I would use an icon instead of having color be significant, but I'm sure you would probably have done that already if it were a simple addition (and it's certainly less elegant than colours).

This game has really pretty simple patterning outside of certain storyline and happy events. Girls alternate Dorm Event / Other location event, though not always predictably (eg sometimes you get dorm other other dorm, and so on). A minority of events only trigger on weekends. Most of the time, if a girl's stuck and not advancing it's because the next event is a joint event and requires a different girl to be advanced before it can fire (because it involves both of them being at a certain point). The storyline in this game is actually completely linear and there are not actually any optional events at all; even 'side' girl events have to be completed, and you can't advance out of chapter 1 until you have completed everything. The only missable or optional events are some happy scenes (just a couple, most are also mandatory)

This can cause you to get stuck if you actually need something else to advance, and there are a couple very large joint events that require a whole host of other events to be completed before they can fire (for example, there's a beach trip that requires something like 8 different girls to be advanced to the correct stage before it will actually happen).

Consequently, it is usually not possible to focus on a single girl and max her storyline completely while ignoring the others. You will eventually encounter joint events that require the other participants to be advanced as well.

It initially seems like this isn't the case because some girls you are very likely to advance with initially (like Ayane and Chika) do not have a lot of event gating until later on. But in reality, this isn't a sandbox game with optional choices - every girl is required to advance, and there are only a couple situations where Sensei makes a meaningful decision or the order that you do stuff matters (good homie/bad homie is the primary one of these, and is one you'll run afoul of if you rapidly advance Chika's storyline early in the game).

Currently, there's not any event in the game that requires more than 30-35 affection or 15 lust. If you're being blocked, it isn't a grind issue: it's a you not having done other events issue.

Most of the pre-requisites are obvious and trackable to which girls are friends or roommates with others: Rin and Futaba, Ayane and Sana or Ami, Ami and Maya, Chika and Yumi, etc. More complex events may require more (as I mentioned, beach vacation requires basically every girl to be advanced to a certain point before it happens, and completing chapter 1 and starting chapter 2 requires literally all ch1 events to have taken place)

Its unlikely that the tracker will ever tell you what you have to do because this game features puzzles that have to be solved, including a couple that lock you into infinite loops until you solve them. This game has horror/psychological/existential crisis tags for a reason.

You can't make things go better for Rin at the beach, but you can make Rin not resent you for that result. If you let the beach event happen and then proceed down Chika's path, she won't be upset with you for it. The game tracks this as a flag called "badhomie". It affects your ongoing relationship with Rin.

IMO it is a shitty gotcha because its possible to advance Chika's storyline past the point of no return before she explicitly tells you about her crush. It's not just one of the few decisions with an impact, but it's one where you can be unaware of that impact when you do it. The later Chika events do NOT require you to have progressed Rin's route to the point she explicitly tells you about her crush on Chika. Generally, this game doesn't do that kind of thing.

To whit:



label mall:
if chika_love >= 0 and firsttimemall == False:
jump firsttimemall
if chika_love >= 5 and mall5 == False:
jump mall5
if chika_love >= 10 and mall10 == False:
jump mall10
if chika_love >= 15 and chikadorm15 == True and day79 == True and mall15 == False:
jump mall15
if chika_love >= 20 and chikadorm20 == True and mall20 == False:
jump mall20
elif christmas7 == True:
jump mallgen2
else:
jump mall2to4

"Hang out":
if chika_love >= 5 and day == 1 and chikadorm5 == False:
"I should probably wait until Yumi's not right there to hang out with Chika..."
jump doorknock
if chika_love >= 5 and day != 1 and day != 3 and chikadorm5 == False:
jump chikadorm5
if chika_love >= 10 and mall10 == True and chikadorm5 == True and chikadorm10 == False:
jump chikadorm10
if chika_love >= 15 and chikadorm10 == True and chikadorm15 == False and day != 3 and day != 1:
jump chikadorm15
if chika_love >= 20 and mall15 == True and chikadorm20 == False:
jump chikadorm20
else:
jump chikadormgen


As you can see, none of those depend on Rin's events. This one has always really bugged me as unfair, as the first time I played I finished Chika's whole route before I started Rin's, and it felt like a gotcha that didn't make any sense (it's not betraying her when you don't even know yet). IMO, Selebus should require cafe15 to do Chikadorm20, so the player has some kind of knowledge of what they're potentially doing. Most of the time these kinds of pathing problems are caught by the central story events (Day79 in this case), but Day79 itself only requires Chickadorm15. The game is just assuming that you have advanced Rin to Cafe15 in the first 79 days, but it's quite possible to not do that.

IMO it's the biggest continuity/logic issue in the game.

Exactly this. Betraying Rin does lock you out of some events even though she "forgives" sensei, but it also opens up one of the best written scenes in the game and gives Sensei his first actual consequence for his extremely unethical and illegal activities. Calling it a bad outcome may be true from a gameplay perspective but as a reader I'm enjoying both paths (although I haven't seen Rin's new events and probably won't until March).

I really think this game is best enjoyed if you lean into the writing rather than treating it purely as a game. While there is a gameplay loop, you aren't always going to be rewarded for engaging with it and sometimes that may not play out until a dozen updates later.

One thing I'm really looking forward to is watching people play this for the first time when it's finished just to see how that experience differs from ours. What Selebus has done better than any other developer I've seen on here is make the storytelling a part of the development process. One of the reasons I think a lot of people went after Chika first is they saw the pink event on her timeline and none on Rin's, it'll be interesting to see if more players catch the badhomie trap when the game is finished.

This game has really pretty simple patterning outside of certain storyline and happy events. Girls alternate Dorm Event / Other location event, though not always predictably (eg sometimes you get dorm other other dorm, and so on). A minority of events only trigger on weekends. Most of the time, if a girl's stuck and not advancing it's because the next event is a joint event and requires a different girl to be advanced before it can fire (because it involves both of them being at a certain point). The storyline in this game is actually completely linear and there are not actually any optional events at all; even 'side' girl events have to be completed, and you can't advance out of chapter 1 until you have completed everything. The only missable or optional events are some happy scenes (just a couple, most are also mandatory)

This can cause you to get stuck if you actually need something else to advance, and there are a couple very large joint events that require a whole host of other events to be completed before they can fire (for example, there's a beach trip that requires something like 8 different girls to be advanced to the correct stage before it will actually happen).

Consequently, it is usually not possible to focus on a single girl and max her storyline completely while ignoring the others. You will eventually encounter joint events that require the other participants to be advanced as well.

It initially seems like this isn't the case because some girls you are very likely to advance with initially (like Ayane and Chika) do not have a lot of event gating until later on. But in reality, this isn't a sandbox game with optional choices - every girl is required to advance, and there are only a couple situations where Sensei makes a meaningful decision or the order that you do stuff matters (good homie/bad homie is the primary one of these, and is one you'll run afoul of if you rapidly advance Chika's storyline early in the game).

Currently, there's not any event in the game that requires more than 30-35 affection or 15 lust. If you're being blocked, it isn't a grind issue: it's a you not having done other events issue.

Most of the pre-requisites are obvious and trackable to which girls are friends or roommates with others: Rin and Futaba, Ayane and Sana or Ami, Ami and Maya, Chika and Yumi, etc. More complex events may require more (as I mentioned, beach vacation requires basically every girl to be advanced to a certain point before it happens, and completing chapter 1 and starting chapter 2 requires literally all ch1 events to have taken place)

Its unlikely that the tracker will ever tell you what you have to do because this game features puzzles that have to be solved, including a couple that lock you into infinite loops until you solve them. This game has horror/psychological/existential crisis tags for a reason.

But in reality, this isn't a sandbox game with optional choices - every girl is required to advance, and there are only a couple situations where Sensei makes a meaningful decision or the order that you do stuff matters (good homie/bad homie is the primary one of these, and is one you'll run afoul of if you rapidly advance Chika's storyline early in the game).
Currently, there's not any event in the game that requires more than 30-35 affection or 15 lust.  If you're being blocked, it isn't a grind issue: it's a you not having done other events issue.
Most of the pre-requisites are obvious and trackable to which girls are friends or roommates with others: Rin and Futaba, Ayane and Sana or Ami,  Ami and Maya, Chika and Yumi, etc.  More complex events may require more (as I mentioned, beach vacation requires basically every girl to be advanced to a certain point before it happens, and completing chapter 1 and starting chapter 2 requires literally all ch1 events to have taken place)

Example, Rin's first event after the beach changes depending on whether you were a good or a bad homie to her.

Python: 
text ("{color=#AF7F00}Birthday: May 9th{/color}") style "profile"

Python: 
style profile:

Python:

Only thing different are the color code (which is perfectly normal and valid) and the month/day being displayed (which shouldn't change anything).

Antidepressants are a medication used outside of bipolar disorder for depression and many other issues. I'm on them IRL for insomnia as they are supposed to have a sedative effect that can help one sleep without going into full blown sedatives, which can be dangerous to the user without medical supervision and proper knowledge of how to use them.

Therapy after an incident that leaves mental/emotional trauma is also not uncommon, especially if that trauma leads to depression. In fact, therapy is one of the first steps to proper treatment of depression, bipolar disorder present or not.

It is also often a step avoided by those who suffer from depression for reasons like the ones Rin uses as justification to herself to act normal when she is clearly suffering instead of seeking the help of those around her. If not for her foster parents, Rin might not have been alive in the game because they forced her into therapy for her own good, something she is admittedly grateful to them for.

Depression is one of the major causes of suicide with those who go that far often refusing to seek help for some personal reason like not wanting people to worry, not wanting people to dislike them, not wanting to be treated differently, stuff like that.

Okay, from the sound of it, you're currently stuck on "There is Nothing" under the Main Events category. Trying to go through the events on the wiki can be a bit of a rabbit hole, but you can eventually figure out what you need to do to complete each one. Go ahead and set "Semblance of a Soul" aside for now. This event auto-triggers at 10 lust after you have completed the Christmas events. The way you can find this information (at least on a desktop browser like Chrome), is spread across a couple different sections on the Event's wiki page.

  1. There is a box near the top right of every event's wiki page that lists the info and technical info of each event. Under the technical information section, you'll find the event's requirements (in the case of "Semblance of a Soul", the requirements are Makoto 10 Lust and having already seen "Fireworks, Chicken, and the Innate Fear of Death" which is the last Christmas Event.
  2. A little further down the page is the Criteria section which lists how you can get (aka activate) the event and how you can miss the event (Here, it is stated that "Semblance of a Soul" triggers automatically on a weekday if the requirements are met and that missing the event is not possible).
Without an upload of your save or more information on what events you're missing for all the girls, it's hard to know exactly what you need to trigger "There is Nothing" to finish chapter 1 and start the Christmas events. The way I go about checking my save is by going to the page of the event I'm stuck on, checking I meet the requirements, and then checking I meet the parts under the "To Get This Event" subsection.

For "There is Nothing", you need to make sure that you have the event listed under the "To Get This Event" subsection for each girl complete, as well as every event before it. You can quickly do this by going into each girls' page in-game, pulling up their event list, finding their corresponding event listed in "There is Nothing", and making sure that event and every event prior is either green with a checkmark next to it or red with a line through it.

It is and I wholeheartedly suggest trying it out. The typical model is a horror story where the catalyst for the events that occur are based on familiar people acting in unfamiliar, yet seemingly orchestrated ways. Stories where the world seems to have gone mad; and the protagonist is not necessarily an exception. The name comes from the idea that electromagnetic waves (denpa) is causing people to act strangely (although it is rarely anything that mundane).

Most routes will end in some level of sadness or other negative emotions and there is likely to be no truly happy ending at all or, if there is, only one that will come as the final route to be developed.

As for a game for 'just fapping,' no, this is not that kind of game. There is going to be very little in the way of sexy time with any of the characters and it will be slow burn for some of them. When each girl becomes open and ready for sex is entirely dependent on the kind of person they are. The ones with stronger moral views on sex or who are introverted and quiet are likely to take a long time to get there while the rest are likely to take less time. This game is entirely story driven in this aspect. The girl has to say she's ready and offer herself to the MC before the sexy times will start, that is, unless Selebus is willing to add rape, which I'm not so sure he is given he had multiple chances already.

Also, 'just fapping' is actually likely to get you stuck. In this game, you really should pay attention to every single detail as some of it will come up later in ways that will get you stuck.

posts.content_html_raw:
Hey, Selebus.

First thing, kudos for making an absolutely great game. I'm a big fan of VNs, and this is without a doubt one of the best written VNs I've ever played --- Eastern or Western -- and I've played a lot, so that's a big compliment. I'm only maybe halfway through the released content so far, so I'll have more to say and theories to share after I catch up.

I have a suggestion though. I've seen other people having a problem with the scary scenes being a bit too scary, and I saw how one person suggested you allow the option to remove them and you shot that down because they're the whole point of the game. I totally get that. But I thought of an option you could include for the scaredy cats like myself to also fully enjoy the game.

In either the option menu or as a cheat code in the computer, perhaps you could include the option to insert a "jump scare warning" before a scary scene starts? If it happens in the normal flow of a scene you could maybe have a little countdown thing appear showing it'll happen in 3 clicks, then 2, then 1. And if the scary scene appears based off of something the user clicks on (and they've activated the warning option), perhaps you could put the little smiley face thing next to it so they'd know to prepare themselves for it.

I totally get that this will lessen the impact of the scene, which is why it should be off by default and 100% optional. It's something that probably the majority of users would not want to turn on. But for people that are weaker to this sort of thing, it could be really helpful, and not make them do things like quit playing, or play with no sound, or the like.

That first happy scene was kind of mildly traumatic for me, as my guard was just totally down and it came out of nowhere and made me not want to play anymore. Since then I've extensively used a walkthrough, played with the sound way down, and kind of been completely willing to spoil myself by reading this thread (despite typically hating spoilers), to lessen the impact and surprise of the sudden scary scenes. An option like this would allow me, and others like me, to play in a more normal way.

I wouldn't say anything if I felt I was the only one that'd benefit from something like this, but I've seen a lot of other people posting in this thread about having a similar feeling that the scary bits are too much for them, so I thought this may be something that could be beneficial for many others as well.

Thanks for the consideration. Even if you change nothing I'll still be playing this damn thing to the end because it's too damn good. But I thought I'd share my idea. And again, thank you for making this, because it kicks ass.

I've seen other people having a problem with the scary scenes being a bit too scary, and I saw how one person suggested you allow the option to remove them and you shot that down because they're the whole point of the game.  I totally get that.  But I thought of an option you could include for the scaredy cats like myself to also fully enjoy the game.
In either the option menu or as a cheat code in the computer, perhaps you could include the option to insert a "jump scare warning" before a scary scene starts?  If it happens in the normal flow of a scene you could maybe have a little countdown thing appear showing it'll happen in 3 clicks, then 2, then 1.  And if the scary scene appears based off of something the user clicks on (and they've activated the warning option), perhaps you could put the little smiley face thing next to it so they'd know to prepare themselves for it.
I totally get that this will lessen the impact of the scene, which is why it should be off by default and 100% optional.  It's something that probably the majority of users would not want to turn on.  But for people that are weaker to this sort of thing, it could be really helpful, and not make them do things like quit playing, or play with no sound, or the like.
That first happy scene was kind of mildly traumatic for me, as my guard was just totally down and it came out of nowhere and made me not want to play anymore.  Since then I've extensively used a walkthrough, played with the sound way down, and kind of been completely willing to spoil myself by reading this thread (despite typically hating spoilers), to lessen the impact and surprise of the sudden scary scenes.  An option like this would allow me, and others like me, to play in a more normal way.
I wouldn't say anything if I felt I was the only one that'd benefit from something like this, but I've seen a lot of other people posting in this thread about having a similar feeling that the scary bits are too much for them, so I thought this may be something that could be beneficial for many others as well.
Thanks for the consideration.  Even if you change nothing I'll still be playing this damn thing to the end because it's too damn good.  But I thought I'd share my idea.  And again, thank you for making this, because it kicks ass.

Click to expand...
He does and most of the info can either be found in the game itself, there's an about section on the main menu, or through playing them in programs like VLC, which display the actual information like the real title, if available, in the title bar of the window.

kloklo said:
So a couple things about the recent updates:
1. I really like that it looks like the MC is showing a little bit more care for the girls and their wellbeing and happiness (even if its just a little bit)
2. I like that there have been several instances of the MC saying that he's bad...but not that bad, in reference to some darker topics here and there, which kinda helps not feel like a monster with all the stuff the we have the MC do
3. I went through the Rin content first before the Molly stuff and I just want to say....
I really hope there isn't another schadenfreude situation like with Rin and Chika earlier because I can't take much more of these smol beans being hurt like that, I just want everyone to be happy
4. The main reason I still play is because the end of the description of the game is "But don't worry! Everything will be okay~" and I really just want to see it through to the end and see everyone okay at the end of it all.
Click to expand...
I could honestly see that happening again with Molly, that was definitely not a one off scenario. This is a Denpa game, happy is just not in the cards except as maybe a true end scenario.

Vertius said:
Please tell me this scene means what I think it does... Maya is one of my favorite female characters of all time... hands down, and although I would never trade the slow build that's been happening for anything 'cause it was amazing and her interactions with Sensei are hilarious, I'm also super excited for the chance to finally break through
her shell a little bit.

View attachment 1051308
Click to expand...
Whatever you think it means, it probably doesn't. Maya is one of the girls with the furthest to go, only second to Yumi, who is progressing faster than Maya.

demondelic.psy said:
1. Me too, albeit for me it doesn't really make me like Sensei that much more. He's certainly got his moments with the girls that warms me up to a wholesome degree.
2. It's easier to admit your fault than it is to change anything about them, on that I can relate with the guy but as I've said it doesn't takeaway from the fact that he's an asshole.
3. Yeah that whole scene hit me like a truck because I felt closer to Rin than most in this VN, Yumi being the closest.
4. I'm hoping for something like that too but at this point if you've gone through as many tragic stories as I have you'll come to not expect the good stories to have a happy ending. It's always been that kind of expectation for me and this VN doesn't stray from that mindset. If anything I just hope it doesn't hurt as bad. I'd love to be proven wrong once this all comes full circle.
Click to expand...
1. I certainly don't see him as I did originally, but I still don't like him as a person.

2. Indeed

3. That was totally unexpected in a very good way. It almost makes me want to up my subscription just because Selebus deserves it, but alas I cannot...yet.

4. Yeah, no, Denpa games don't typically do that. On top of that, this is said to be the dark route, which is likely to be the worst of the bunch in terms of positive or negative.

demondelic.psy said:
Maya and Sensei share a deeper history than it is initially stated. Or at least that's what I've felt like. It's a stupid mistake on my part too correlate Happy Events with their Main and Character Branch counterparts but at this point I honestly feel the connection between those two. It's there and slowly but assuredly since not many things have been going to how she thought was predicted, we're seeing her shell slowly crack. Even if that doesn't mean we'll get any closer to her, I'm hoping to see more vulnerable sides like this in the upcoming future.
Click to expand...
Some here believe they might have been romantically involved or even sexually involved and that her one scene so far is likely a past event with her and old Sensei from before she went all gloom and doom.

JMccovery said:
I'm at the point where whenever there's the slightest bit of static, or the music becomes strange, I'm in full alert mode. But yet, I'm okay with it, and actually want more.

I haven't had this kind of trepidation towards a game in a very, very long time. Not since the Kingdom of Zeal and the Ocean Palace in Chrono Trigger (I seriously stop playing for a while when I get to Zeal, feelings are way too strong there).
Click to expand...
Same, it's like I developed a Selebus sense.

No cap, but this game is hella depressing and very cryptic for being very straightforward(?)

Yep, Denpa games in a nutshell.

After LiL, probably not (Unless the prequel stretch goal is hit on Patreon).
I might do girl-focused, Sensei-less special events as additional holiday type updates, but that's something that's probably still a ways off.
After LiL, I'll likely go back to 2D.
Game is noooooowhere near finished yet, though, so that's still years away.
Click to expand...
You know that's probably going to happen now that you've said that, right? Kind of like a reverse jinx.

posts.content_html_raw:
Just want to point out two very interesting statistics from this month that once again reiterate how leaking content does not help games.

13p1 - Release does not leak at all. Game experiences the largest post-release spike in support so far despite adding far less content than usual.

13p2 - Release leaks within 12 hours. Game experiences the smallest spike in support so far and February becomes the first month in LiL history without a net gain, despite being one of the strongest updates so far.

Please support the developers you like if possible. It’s one thing to download leaked versions of games, but literally begging for someone else to buy it and share it with you so you can save $5 can be incredibly damaging to developers.

I’m lucky enough to be making good money off of LiL, but that doesn’t mean it isn’t disheartening seeing things like this. Especially after working so hard to provide consistent, quality content in a more than reasonable amount of time at a more than reasonable cost.

alex2011 said:
It is and I wholeheartedly suggest trying it out. Without going into details specific to this game, this is what is called a Denpa game, I'll just quote from VNDB on this as I am not always the best at putting things correctly, not dyslexic or anything like that, I just don't always have the easiest time getting the point across.


There is one event in the 'happy' scenes category, that's the category where the horror tag comes from for this game, that does seem to spook some people, but most of it is just weird, not actually scary. There are also some things that happen without a choice where even the MC doesn't seem to be in control. You'll know them when you see them as it gets acknowledged in the text.

Also keep in mind that, while VNDB doesn't say it, Denpa is known for not having a very happy tone to it. Most routes will end in some level of sadness or other negative emotions and there is likely to be no truly happy ending at all or, if there is, only one that will come as the final route to be developed.

As for a game for 'just fapping,' no, this is not that kind of game. There is going to be very little in the way of sexy time with any of the characters and it will be slow burn for some of them. When each girl becomes open and ready for sex is entirely dependent on the kind of person they are. The ones with stronger moral views on sex or who are introverted and quiet are likely to take a long time to get there while the rest are likely to take less time. This game is entirely story driven in this aspect. The girl has to say she's ready and offer herself to the MC before the sexy times will start, that is, unless Selebus is willing to add rape, which I'm not so sure he is given he had multiple chances already.

Also, 'just fapping' is actually likely to get you stuck. In this game, you really should pay attention to every single detail as some of it will come up later in ways that will get you stuck.

Also, it is recommended NOT to try for a single girl, those routes aren't in the game yet and that will only get you stuck by not having a girl you weren't going after leveled enough for required events to trigger. It is recommended that you grind them all as equally as possible on this route.

It is going to be a while yet before single girl routes are even started, this is one of the general routes, the 'dark' route, which will likely have the most negative of the possible endings.

posts.content_html_raw:
One final thing I've been thinking about. Sorry if my spamming the thread with a bunch of posts in a row is annoying anyone.

I saw some people earlier in the thread suggesting that Sensei wasn't so bad of a guy because he could choose to do good or do bad. We're the ones to blame if he chooses bad. I have a few counter points to this.

1. There are forced actions and forced thoughts that imply extreme cruelty and a complete lack of empathy in his heart. It's not always there, but it sometimes is, and I don't think normal people really go to the places he goes to in his mind so often.

2. The very fact that he seems to see the potential for evil actions in so many situations seems to suggest that he's extremely capable of those evil actions. A good person all alone with a girl doesn't suddenly entertain the idea of raping her, for example. The choice wouldn't even exist if they were a good-hearted person. (Not that I've encountered a choice like this -- though I have seen him thinking along these lines --- but just the fact that bad choices are available tells us about the character)

3. This theory is more about a person that's done awful things and is now regretting it, and being thrown into situations where he has a chance to do them again in some kind of dream state. So it makes sense that he can either choose to do better or continue to do awful things this time. Because you can choose to do right this time doesn't suggest that he was also innocent before.

2.  The very fact that he seems to see the potential for evil actions in so many situations seems to suggest that he's extremely capable of those evil actions.  A good person all alone with a girl doesn't suddenly entertain the idea of raping her, for example.  The choice wouldn't even exist if they were  a good-hearted person.  (Not that I've encountered a choice like this -- though I have seen him thinking along these lines --- but just the fact that bad choices are available tells us about the character)

posts.content_html_raw:
TL;DR Player Sensei is orignial sensei, HOPE is Sensei & Maya's dead hopes, a Nozomu is you and everything is terrible.

My personal take is that Player Sensei is original Sensei, but without active access to his memories beyond general ideas of how his childhood was. My justification for this is the fact that sometimes it seems that the "old" Sensei "takes over" (like with the anniversary of Ami's parent's death). Before the start of what I'm gonna call for the sake of convinience the "first" loop (the one we arrive in after we jump) I think there were a slew of other Senseis, which is why Maya is so convinced that we're one of them.

All the Senseis that Maya has known have done roughly the same things, barely lasting even one reset. Maybe these other Senseis flirted with their students and tried to get more intimate with them, but I don't think that any of them succeeded (my reasoning here being that Ami, Ayane and Makoto's virginities don't reset with the world, and Ayane is entirely down for some action day 1 so if anyone could take her then she wouldn't have managed to keep her hymen).

The reason I think that none of them succeeded is because the girls could tell that Sensei was different. Notice that most people don't seem to notice that Sensei is acting differently under our control, only Maya who can remember each of the loops seems to notice that we're acting radically differently from the Senseis before us (she noticed that we were a new person right away after all). Add on top of this the fact that Maya has been almost constantly noticing that we're doing things differently from the other Senseis (saying stuff like "that's never happened before") and it builds a suspicion in my mind.

There's a reason for the first "choice" in this game, and the latest Happy event shows us why. I believe that Maya and original Sensei were in a relationship; someone found out, potentially ruining both their lives. Orignial sensei genuinely loved Maya (and visa versa) and wanted the best for her and so decided to take drastic measures to protect her from the inevitable scandal of a teacher and his student being in a relationship. I'm not saying that this was a rational choice, anyone subscribing to the "player Sensei = original Sensei" theory will know that player Sensei has a whole bunch of mental issues. Combining these with the need to protect something he loves could lead to irrational decisions being made.

Saying this, I don't think the jump happened in front of Maya, as depicted in the happy scene it's shown in. I'm not sure Maya knows what happened to original Sensei.

My justification for Maya genuinely loving original Sensei is in the event where you buy her a scarf (there being several instances of a "girl with a green scarf" in splashscreen text) she basically breaks down in this event, feelings that she thought long dead over (presumably) thousands of resets suddenly coming back and hitting her. All for a man she "knows" to not be the one she fell in love with.

Now, as for what's happening in regards to the game world, I think it's probably more simple than it looks or has been speculated to be. We have confirmation of three (at the very least) god-like entities, HOPE, Nozomu and the wire god. We also know that "god is dead" which I think refers to Nozomu. What we know about Nozomu is that he created all life to effectively use as onaholes then got pissed off when they started fucking each other. So long as we're generous with the definition of "create" this could be a stand-in for the player (not Sensei, YOU) think about how many people on this forum alone get pissed off when the groups of pixels with a name and dialogue get any action with anyone other than the group of pixels with a name and dialogue THEY control (note: I am pretty much one of these people too).

As for the wire god, it could be the machine the game is running on? I honestly don't know. But Tsuneyo's recent comments about dead people turning into trees and the fact her father is on a complex life-support machine (and her constant glitching and HOPE's face on her PJs) makes me pretty suspicious of her and her father's circumstances.

I honestly have no idea about HOPE. Though saying that there are two characters in the game who seem to have little to no hope, they being Sensei and Maya. Sensei doesn't have any attachment to anything at this point so has no real reason to hope for the future and Maya KNOWS that there is no future (and has known it for potentially thousands of years at this point). So maybe HOPE is a manifestation of their combined dead hopes (god is dead after all). This would also explain why HOPE hates incest, that coming from Maya's suspicion and jealousy towards Ami impacting her hope for a future together with Sensei.

Anyway, this is already a huge fucking wall of text, so I'ma stop here. If anyone's got anything that I've forgotten to refute or support this I'd be grateful

Harem Route (You are here) | Dark Route | Purity Routes (Endings) | True End

The harem route will lead into the dark route no matter what. There will be no true harem ending.
The dark route will end with the option to pursue a purity route for any character in the game.
Purity routes will come out one at a time and add a load of new content for whichever girl you choose. The order these will come out in will likely be chosen at random.
Finishing one purity route will give you the option to start a new game directly from where you choose who to pursue so you won't have to play the game all over again just to get there.
The true end of the game will unlock only after all of the purity routes have been completed.

morty2301 said:
so are some character scenes locked until I do other girls, like I haven't been interested in the sports girl, and have amis stats up super high but no new scene is happening
Click to expand...
Yes, there are requirements that involve unlocking other girls' scenes, which is why it is suggested to raise them all as equally as possible even if it isn't a girl you don't want to pursue. In fact, based on comments similar to your case, most of the time this issue crops up is due to a girl the player didn't want to go for, not that there's anything wrong with that beyond the getting stuck part, just an interesting observation. Side girls are also needed in some cases, so make sure those ones are leveled. Also, don't go too high on affection or you might end up locking yourself into a situation where you automatically trigger an event you don't want to trigger until another event passes because that can sometimes cause a bad outcome. There is only one such case right now and it does require you to go to a certain place, but it is not safe to say there will not be more later or that future ones won't just trigger on affection alone.

Hey everyone, I dont want to offtop, but given the nature of what I want to say, writing it here seems natural.

I want to thank you guys a lot. Especially Selebus, for creating this masterpiece, but also the community. Why? Let me explain:
I wanted to start developing my own games, tell the stories through this media for a long, long time. But I always held myself back, saying: It is not for me, I am better at playing than creating, it will not be good, people will not like it etc. After I played LiL and later found this comunity I started to belive in myself. I played this wonderful game, I saw this awesome community, and it motivated me a lot. Now, after all this time I finally decided to start my own project. It will be a long road before the first release, but I started. And it matters. And I have you to thank for this. I wanted to write this message here to thank all of you guys, for inspiration, and for helping me believe in myself!

And, like I said before - especially BIG thanks to Selebus!

posts.content_html_raw:
God I have the absolute most love-hate relationship with this game. The writing is incredibly top-notch, but I feel completely blue-balled every time I play it. This is like the 30th update and Yumi still doesn't have a sexual scene, and I shudder the amount of time it would take to reach sexual content for any of the new characters(I know that Molly got hers, but it's not really directed at the MC).

Still, the characters are so incredibly well developed that it's just so emotionally satisfying to play this. Playing the end of Rin's route(no spoilers), I felt so...happy with how it turned out for her and the MC. I can't imagine the catharsis that would come out from Yumi's storyline(as well as a more complete version of Rin), but the hours put into to have a single kiss...and I can't even be mad because that's why it's so interesting.

TBH, I'd like to see longer updates with a longer hiatus because I'd really like to see the original main cast storyline get updated a lot more(Yumi, Miku Maya Rin etc) rather than having new updates be solely focused on fleshing out the new characters. They're great and all, but the game put up so much emotional build-up for these characters that it's frustrating when it just...ends there.

Well, I am more shocked that it was "unprovoked" and confused me a lot, so, I am looking forward to understand what exactly made this possible in the first place since as of now there is nothing that make that much of a "deal breaker" to do that.
Click to expand...
Let me start by saying I'm not a psychologist, but have been in a similar position to Makoto about 13 years ago.

I believe there was no one "deal breaker." It seems to me like a few small things that just wore her down over time. She was really close to her father, with him being her main emotional support, but he left for the space war. Her mother admits to being really bad at emotional support stuff and Makoto seems to dislike how similar she is to her mother in terms of sexuality. The main person she looked up to and wanted to be like was Sensei, but then he became super lazy and started teasing and messing with her. Finally, she holds herself to a very high standard and, with Sensei becoming so lazy, has put an immense amount of pressure on herself basically taking over his job while maintaining excellent grades to eventually become a teacher herself.

Normally none of this would lead to suicide on its own, but combining the immense amount of pressure she's put herself under, all the authority figures in her life pushing her to be more sexual when she dislikes that aspect of herself, and having no one to give her the emotional support she needs (she tries with Sensei several times, but he doesn't get it and ends up teasing her and/or making it worse), it eventually just wore her down until a moment of weakness when she just wanted to escape from her situation, and jumping was the only answer she could see.

Like i said, I saw it coming because she cries out for help on several occasions before Bluejay. However, they're all subtle enough that they can easily be misinterpreted as something else, or something else is distracting from them each time. The only reason I picked up on them was because I had done similar things. Thankfully for me, my mother picked up on my cries for help before it was too late. But for Makoto, no one did.

Or I could just be misinterpreting everything.

They make little sense right now because we are at the very beginning of the game, this game is not even close to finished despite what the number says, they'll make sense as things start to come together. Also, I never said there was zero chance. The main story of the game is like two sides of a coin. On the one you have the light-hearted events, on the other you have the doom and gloom. Both are the main story with the light stuff being what is happening on the surface while the doom and gloom simmers underneath, unknown to the characters until it comes out via certain character events and in the 'happy' scene events.

The only person who ever knows the full story before the rest of us would be the developer himself once he is on the final build, but before he releases it. Without the full story, things are going to make little sense. For most of us, it actually piques our interest and is the reason some of us theorize what will happen to varying degrees of success.

Suffering and not having happier events are not the same, they can happen separately or together. In this case, they are only suffering now because there is no way to help them get out of their mental situation now. That will likely change even if things don't necessarily become sunshine and rainbows. It could mean that they no longer suffer from their issues, like Rin overcomes her depression, but they still feel long term aftereffects from it because they were afflicted for such a long time. It could be that they never get cured, but the MC is there to stop things from getting worse. At this point, nobody knows how it will happen, only what the common path of a Denpa game means for the possibilities presented in this one in particular.

I've been at this game for a while, I didn't really have any interests in the game at first glance but quickly fell victim to in love with it afterwards.

The script is opposite of plain and boring, it always livens up the dialogues and often shows the inner thoughts of Sensei,
the characters feel alive and real, what they say can be felt and relatable,
the amount of texts is just right to read and not skip through,
the hex figures, "out of context" events and randomly deformed images can cause me paranoia,
contains some deep quotes about the interesting view point about this world,
wording is realistic and practical, plenty of jokes to laugh at......

-that's page 1 of 5 (I can go on for more)-​

So anyway, good job Lebus
